notes: Grinding slimes with a sword for coins and spending them at a settlement is RPG's combat-and-economy loop, and its wording for world-open — town, roads and mob clearings all on one surface — is the whole map this prompt describes; Simulation is named second because the city genuinely grows by purchase like a tycoon, but its plot shapes would have thrown away the monster ground and its gate wording is about paying for buttons rather than what is asked here. No preset survived: Open World & Survival RPG was closest by premise, fighting and building a base in an open world, but its biome shape brings a P4 split this single map does not want and its gathering nodes have no counterpart when coins come off kills, which leaves the shape swapped and most options dropped. Two things I decided without a user: the wall is a city wall, so the settlement reads as ground the slimes stay out of, and the windows and doors are facade detail rather than enterable rooms, which keeps this off P3. The city area starts empty and fills in as buildings and walls are bought, per the author's answer, and 'a large map with such a terrain' is what puts natural relief in and moves the route to tiered.
